article_title: Scaffolding competence-based learning design in the dental simulation curriculum.
citation: Foxton Richard, San Diego Jonathan P., Lu Emily, Rajadurai Susha, Bartlett Anitha, McIlwane Clare, Austin Rupert, Srisontisuk Pinsuda, Sagoo Anika K., Piper Kim. (2025). Scaffolding competence‐based learning design in the dental simulation curriculum. European Journal of Dental Education. https://doi.org/10.1111/eje.12985
title: Paired dental simulation fidelity labs: haptics (SIMtoCARE) and phantom-head (A-dec) environments
description: The faculty operates two dental simulation fidelity labs used in the undergraduate curriculum. FL18-A houses 18 SIMtoCARE haptic task-trainer simulators with digital audio-visual technologies, integrating a phantom-head interface for a blended augmented reality learning experience, where teachers can demonstrate and observe students. FL20-B is fully integrated with 90 A-dec phantom heads, AV facilities and intra-oral scanners, offering a digitally augmented workflow combining lecture and laboratory as a complementary environment.
requirements: Both simulator types and AV facilities to support demonstration, observation and hands-on exercises
target_learning_goals: hands-on clinical skills exercises, tutorials and demonstrations in restorative dentistry
examples: Teachers can provide a demonstration using one of the SIMtoCARE simulators and observe students perform exercises
key_sources: Foxton Richard, San Diego Jonathan P., Lu Emily, Rajadurai Susha, Bartlett Anitha, McIlwane Clare, Austin Rupert, Srisontisuk Pinsuda, Sagoo Anika K., Piper Kim. (2025). Scaffolding competence‐based learning design in the dental simulation curriculum. European Journal of Dental Education. https://doi.org/10.1111/eje.12985

article_title: Mathematics and incentives in the slums
citation: G. Stefansson, J. Lentin, A. H. Jonsdottir, E. Eiríksson, A. Kristjánsson. (2022). Mathematics and Incentives in the Slums. https://libraries.tutor-web.net/
title: KCSE-targeted drill module built from exam questions expanded into large randomized drillsets with graded difficulty
description: The tutor-web module targeting the KCSE national exam was built by taking questions from an example exam and writing a computer program for each question, generating "drill sets of 100 drill items for each question." When some exam questions proved far too easy or far too difficult, new batches of deliberately easy and harder drills were added, and items extending the national curriculum were included, designed to be self-explanatory but requiring new thinking, with detailed answers provided after incorrect responses.
requirements: A computer program per exam question to generate drill items in large numbers
Random-number generation of items to avoid direct repetition
Detailed explanations shown immediately after an answer is chosen
constraints: Initially all secondary school drills were based on a single exam, and some of those exam questions were far too easy or far too difficult
The tablet reward is expensive, so curriculum-extending drills were added to require considerable work
target_learners: secondary school students preparing for the KCSE national exam in Kenya
target_learning_goals: passing the KCSE national exam and general mathematical thinking beyond rote learning
examples: Over 50 drillsets for the secondary schools, each with from 100 to several hundred drills; 68 students in Kibera had completed between 1 and 20 drillsets in their starting phase
key_sources: G. Stefansson, J. Lentin, A. H. Jonsdottir, E. Eiríksson, A. Kristjánsson. (2022). Mathematics and Incentives in the Slums. https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.06304

article_title: Prerequisite Relation Learning: A Survey and Outlook
citation: Youheng Bai, Zitao Liu, Teng Guo, Mingliang Hou, and Kui Xiao. 2025. Prerequisite Relation Learning: A Survey and Outlook. ACM Comput. Surv. 57, 11, Article 279. https://doi.org/10.1145/3733593
title: Two granularities of learning resources — knowledge concepts and learning objects — with dual-level prerequisite relations
description: The survey establishes the theoretical foundation by distinguishing two granularities of learning resources. KCs are atomic units of knowledge, while LOs are self-contained educational units encapsulating multiple KCs, formalized through a mapping function M: O → P(K). The IEEE Learning Technology Standards Committee "formally defines a LO as 'any entity, digital or non-digital, that may be used for learning, education, or training'". Prerequisite relations manifest at two levels: KC-to-KC prerequisites within LOs and LO-to-LO module-level dependencies, which underpin different learning approaches — fine-grained concept relationships versus semantic, content-structure-based module relations.
requirements: A mapping between LOs and the KCs they encompass to relate the two levels of prerequisite relations
constraints: Identifying these relations is challenged by diverse resource formats and complex KC-LO relationships, as the survey states
target_learning_goals: defining and organizing prerequisite relations between learning resources
examples: Figure 2 illustrates dual-layer dependencies in mathematics education with LO-level and mapped KC-level prerequisite relations
key_sources: Youheng Bai, Zitao Liu, Teng Guo, Mingliang Hou, and Kui Xiao. 2025. Prerequisite Relation Learning: A Survey and Outlook. ACM Comput. Surv. 57, 11, Article 279. https://doi.org/10.1145/3733593
